assessments.title: Three-argument INSTR runtime entry
assessments.assessment: Canonical ED/1e is INSTR(start, haystack$, needle$): AX carries start, haystack and needle are pushed in that order, and AX carries the result. Four independent binary witnesses span TB 1.0 and 1.1. Adjacent ED/1c is the oracle-verified two-argument INSTR entry; the IR and C runtime already supported arity three.
negative_evidence: Literal and variable CINT probes use inline FISTP/FILD and never ED/1e.
The vendored oracle rejects the common three-argument INSTR source spellings, so this is not oracle-verified.
assessments.implementation: Scanner accepts only canonical ED/1e and the fold consumes the existing AX value plus exactly two string-stack operands.
assessments.source: HANDOFF.md: CLOSED 2026-07-20 — missing runtime-revision three-argument INSTR

assessments.title: RETURN line-target runtime unwind vector
assessments.assessment: Canonical INT 8C followed by a near or short JMP is RETURN <line>: the vector unwinds the active GOSUB/event frame and the jump selects the requested line. Oracle fixture t1_returnline/v10_t1_returnline verifies the source and byte-exact round trip in both dialects.
negative_evidence: One, two, and eight ON KEY declarations did not reproduce the vector.
TB 1.0 keyboard-break toggles, dense KEY ON/OFF control, and simple CLS-plus-assignment handler bodies did not reproduce it.
assessments.promotion_criteria: Satisfied 2026-07-23 by the RETURN <line> oracle fixture and the invariant INT-vector-plus-JMP shape across all five wild hits.
assessments.source: HANDOFF.md: Gap INT-8c — likely ON KEY GOSUB related

assessments.title: Linked CGA snow-avoidance runtime helpers
assessments.assessment: Two complete 116/125-byte helpers are already recognized by full-body fingerprints. Related framed procedures use CGA port 0x3DA, CLI/STI, and direct video-memory writes. This is compiler/runtime-library code, but the source statement or compiler option that links it is unknown.
negative_evidence: No fixture corpus executable contains the helper signature, including ordinary TB 1.0 PRINT programs.
Minimal SCREEN 0, WIDTH 40, and PRINT probes did not link it.
VIEW PRINT and PCOPY are rejected by this Turbo Basic parser.
assessments.implementation: Exact helper bodies produce coverage-only OpaqueHelper IR; this does not claim semantic source recovery.
assessments.promotion_criteria: Identify the source trigger or compiler/runtime option and reproduce a helper byte-exact, or recover authoritative runtime-library provenance.
assessments.source: HANDOFF.md: Gap 19 — byte 06 and REMAINING_GAPS_PLAN.md Wave 3

assessments.title: Unknown runtime system cell 0x8a
assessments.assessment: Confirmed: cell 0x8A (and 0x96, 0xA2 -- the whole COLOR fg/bg + VIEW-border cell family, uniformly +2 from the canonical 0x88/0x94/0xA0/0xAC/0xB8/0xC4) is a runtime-revision-skewed table shift, the same category as RR-NOP-90/RR-NOP-FWAIT/RR-BYTE-EA. No oracle probe (SCREEN mode/colorswitch/page variants, COLOR with/without KEY OFF or DEF SEG, PALETTE) ever produced the shifted offset -- only wild bill.exe and color.exe do, and in both, all three color-cell writes observed there (fg/bg/border) shift by the identical +2, strongly suggesting a whole-table shift in whichever compiler build produced these two EXEs rather than a different statement. The cell only ever feeds COLOR/VIEW/PAINT construction (state.color_cells), so aliasing it to the canonical cell number changes no emitted source -- semantically inert.
assessments.implementation: Closed by session 2026-07-21: core.py's movm_imm/movm_ax system-cell dispatch and arith.py's fp_math FP->int bridge each gained a second branch accepting 0x8A/0x96/0xA2/0xAE/0xBA/0xC6, normalizing to cell-2 before storing into state.color_cells. Closed bill.exe and color.exe fully.

assessments.title: Alternate LINE INPUT encodings
assessments.assessment: The source-level statements are already known, making stable alternate tails or setup sequences plausible runtime-template variants. The two CAL files may be duplicate builds and therefore count as one independent shape until provenance is checked.
assessments.promotion_criteria: Capture complete templates, separate independent builds, and demonstrate that operand and result state match the existing LINE INPUT/LINE INPUT # handlers.

assessments.title: Unidentified runtime dispatcher entries
assessments.assessment: Dispatcher holes are plausible revision-specific entries, but they are equally likely to be ordinary statements or intrinsics not yet identified. Grouping them here is a triage hypothesis, not a shared semantic classification.
assessments.promotion_criteria: Record the complete calling convention and neighboring statement context for each sub independently; promote only entries with cross-file or external runtime evidence.

assessments.title: Far-jump or inline-data pattern
assessments.assessment: Stale: this entry predates the closure. 0xEA is a raw 16-bit `EA off:seg` far transfer; the existing far-call convention (segment-zero offsets rebase from the user-code start, relocated segments use the preceding-byte origin) resolves every non-zero target, and a zero-offset transfer is the fixed cleanup/event handoff that terminates the scan like the existing EC/E8 epilogue. No oracle probe (ERROR/RESUME, ON KEY, ON GOTO, nested IF, GOTO) ever emitted EA, so this remains a wild-only runtime-revision closure, never an oracle fixture.
assessments.implementation: Closed by commit (Far JMP (EA) runtime-revision group, 2026-07-20): scanner records non-zero transfers as `jmpf`; conditional JCC/far-jump pairs use the five-byte skip length.

assessments.title: Compiler-emitted NOP padding
assessments.assessment: Formerly classified as unwitnessable synchronization padding around a CINT-style float-to-int round trip. The scanner now safely decodes literal x86 NOP padding; this is retained to prevent the stale signature from being reopened as an active gap.
assessments.implementation: Closed by commit 631597b (Decode compiler-emitted NOP padding).

assessments.title: IDX% bridge x87-sync marker: bare NOP pair as an fwait alias
assessments.assessment: A follow-on to RR-NOP-90: once the scanner could decode a bare NOP pair generically, electron.exe and rstprint.exe advanced one layer deeper and stopped at the IDX% bridge consumer instead, which only recognized the canonical `fwait` (INT 3D) op at the fistp[0x2C]->movaxmem[0x2C] sync point. A `nop;nop` pair occupies the identical 2-byte span there in both files. Same runtime-revision-skew category as RR-NOP-90/RR-BYTE-EA: no oracle probe (computed row/col, both, explicit CINT()) ever produced the raw NOP pair at this position, only INT 3Dh, so it cannot be fixture-witnessed -- but a NOP is semantically inert and the surrounding bridge is otherwise byte-identical either way, so accepting it as an alias changes no emitted source.
assessments.implementation: Closed by commit 4f29e9b (Decode computed FOR-STEP sign test and runtime-skewed IDX% sync): arith.py's fp_math gained a `_sync_len` helper accepting either 1 op (fwait) or 2 ops (nop;nop) at the sync point, in both the FP->int assign and element-subscript bridge shapes.

assessments.title: DGROUP layout not solvable: large static string array defeats stamp + walk
signatures: DGROUP layout not solvable from the calibrated rules
assessments.assessment: All four files show ZERO candidate stamp matches anywhere in the file (the primary stamp-anchored path in layout.py never fires) and the descending-n walk path also never solves for any n in 0..31. In every file the failure is the SAME shape: a `movsi` disp far beyond anything the walk or any tried static-array record explains (menu.exe 0x400, night.exe 0xa00, sprogh.exe 0x800, swbb.exe 0x1440), read back at the guessed pool position as plain low-value (non-descriptor-tagged) words -- and for menu.exe those movsi disps form a clean, long run of 4-byte-spaced constant-index accesses (0x310..0x400, ~60 entries) immediately after what looks like a cluster of ARR_BLOCK(0x36)-spaced array bases (0x156, 0x18c, 0x1c2, 0x1f8, 0x22e, 0x264). This strongly suggests a static STRING array with a large enough element count (or too many total static arrays, possibly exceeding the stamp's `0<=n<=31` cap) that the current record-parsing/stamp-shape assumptions in `_parse_static_slot`/the stamp search don't hold -- not confirmed to be a runtime-revision issue at all, just an unimplemented or mis-modeled shape. mf.exe fails similarly but with the DISTINCT message 'DGROUP layout not solvable (runtime slot grid anchor)' (has rt_blocks, so it's the grid-anchored path failing instead) -- likely a related but separate cause, not yet checked against this hypothesis.
assessments.promotion_criteria: Hand-derive ds for menu.exe (smallest file of the four) using the ARR_BLOCK-spaced brute-force scan technique from the original gap-16 investigation, confirm whether a big static string array record actually sits where hypothesized, and if so identify what specifically breaks `_parse_static_slot`/the stamp shape for it (element count, rank, or the n<=31 cap) before writing an oracle probe to reproduce a minimal case.
assessments.source: session 2026-07-20, surfaced once the computed-FOR-STEP fix (commit 4f29e9b) let menu.exe's scan reach this far

assessments.title: At least four Turbo Basic runtime builds in the wild corpus; the 1.0 pair differ by one 6-byte block
assessments.assessment: The 16 TB 1.0 programs split into two runtime revisions, and the split is decided by a single block at runtime-region offset 0x1bcf (file 0x1ccf). This oracle's 1.0 spells a 4-way dispatch as `mov bl,[si]; inc si` followed by four `cmp bl,imm8; je` (28 bytes); the other revision spells it `lodsb` followed by four `cmp al,imm8; je` (22 bytes) -- the same routine, hand-shortened by exactly 6 bytes. The fingerprint is clean: all 7 programs at 96-99% build match carry the long form, all 9 at 86-88% carry the short one, with no overlap. A second, independent marker sits at offset 0x0621, where the stack switch loads SS then SP in one revision and SP then SS in the other; it tracks the same split exactly. Those 6 bytes are most of what the positionwise score reacts to. 161 of the differing 16-bit words are CALL rel16 displacements differing by exactly -0x0006, i.e. the same call to a target past the shortened block; a further 22 differ by -0x0020 from a second shortened region in the 0x1d76-0x1fff tail. Measured with alignment instead, the two revisions are 95.5-96% identical (330-370 unreproduced bytes in an 8 KB runtime) against 99.1-99.7% for same-revision programs. So the revision gap is real but small: a handful of size optimizations, not different code. Do NOT read the 0x1500-0x1780 band as a revision marker. It is a table of 16-bit addresses whose entries keep identical spacing but shift per program (autonum -12221, number -5828, rev/book -504): program-specific link-time data, which is why book/number/rev score 96-97% while autonum/baby/banker/mymenu score 99% within the SAME revision. Surveying every program with the dialect-correct reference (the `--all` sweep) shows the corpus holds at least FOUR runtime builds, not two: this oracle's 1.0 and the 6-byte-shorter 1.0 above, plus this oracle's 1.1 and a second 1.1 carrying bill.exe, ck.exe, color.exe and mm.exe. That fourth group scores 18% positionwise and 83.4-83.5% aligned against our 1.1, and its members are 96-99% identical to each other, so it is one coherent build rather than four unrelated ones. It is NOT characterized further -- no fingerprint block has been isolated for it the way `lodsb` isolates the 1.0 split.

assessments.title: Which IDE Options toggles actually put byte-exactness out of reach
assessments.assessment: Audited after the blanket claim 'a program compiled with a toggle can never be reproduced' turned out to be false for Keyboard break. Measured against their default-toggle twins, the flagged corpus fixtures cost: K one byte (the flags mask at prologue-0x73, no code, same length -- fkb_t1_and, fkb_t1_beep); S three bytes plus the mask (fst_t1_gosub); B 128 bytes of instrumentation plus the mask (fbd_t1_arr1); 8087 a different runtime entirely (f87_t1_beep, 86.8% aligned). So K is verifiable with the mask normalized and the rest are not, which is now what verify_wild and verify_fixture implement. The related claim that toggles have NO SOURCE SPELLING is TRUE and was probe-checked here: `$DEBUG`, `$ERROR ON` and `$FLOAT EMULATE` are all rejected by TB 1.1 (Errors 471/416/416), and the metastatements it does accept -- $EVENT, $INCLUDE, $INLINE, $SEGMENT, $SOUND, $STACK -- cover none of the five Options toggles. Scope the remaining exclusion correctly: B/O/S are out of reach OF THIS HARNESS, not in principle. tb_v86.js exposes only --compile-exe/--floppy/--rows/--run-ms/--workspace, but the library underneath drives the IDE by held keystrokes and navigates its menus, so the Options toggles are reachable the same way the compile is. Adding that path would make bill.exe, ck.exe, rstprint.exe and tamstart.exe judgeable -- the only four programs still excluded for a toggle.
